clusters.reason: Identical wording: engaged in active discussion against a specific target, then abstains from the vote.
Identical wording: keeps voting a target after that target defended itself in intense discussion.
Retaliation vote: a player under accusation/questioning/suspicion casts their vote for the very person accusing, questioning, or pushing to eliminate them.
Votes for an accuser whose accusation specifically targeted the voter's own past voting record/consistency.
A player who stayed silent during discussion joins the final consensus/majority lynch vote.
Voter-centric: votes a player the voter personally never voiced any suspicion/criticism of during discussion.
Votes a player they had just been in collaborative/strategic conversation with, having voiced no suspicion of them.
Room-level: votes a target who had not been discussed as a suspect by anyone during the day.
Identical wording: votes for someone who had only just begun participating in the session.
Identical wording: joins a near-unanimous block against a player with a prior controversial interaction.
Identical wording: casts the deciding vote for someone who had challenged the now-dead investigator's credibility.
Identical wording: votes a heavily-scrutinized target without having announced the vote intent earlier.
Identical wording: advocates abstaining on the grounds of insufficient information.
Calls for/urges a decisive, concrete vote to align the group but then abstains.
Proposes an analytical structure/method/exercise for evaluating players or threats, then abstains.
Advocates delaying/waiting on the vote (wait-and-see, wait for more info) rather than deciding now.
Questions the accuser/most-vocal player's basis during discussion, then abstains from the vote.
Casts the lone non-abstaining vote while the rest of the table abstains.
Casts a vote for a target off the room's converging consensus/main-conflict candidate.
Votes a player after spending discussion interrogating/critiquing that player's past voting record.
Votes the player they had been arguing/debating/interrogating with throughout the discussion.
Votes a player they had earlier defended or urged caution about (defense-to-vote reversal).
Votes a player after urging the group not to rely on past voting records/patterns to accuse.
Votes the target designated by an investigator/role claim, following/trusting that claim.
Uses their own role/night-action claim to demand or push the elimination of a specific target.
Votes the consensus/accused target despite having voiced hesitation about the evidence.
Identical wording: pivots to an aggressive vote for a target after previously advocating general caution.
Voiced skepticism about the bandwagon/consensus (its speed, or a pledge to wait) then joins it anyway.
Abstains while citing caution about wrongful elimination / missing/protecting hidden roles.
Announces an intent/inclination to vote a specific player and follows through voting that same player.
Adopts another player's proposed target after voicing agreement with that player's argument.
Abstains after being an active participant in the day's discussion about voting-history.

borderline.note: Voter-never-voiced-suspicion (voter-centric) vs target-not-a-discussed-suspect (room-level) may pick out different moments.
Undiscussed-by-anyone vs merely-not-voiced-by-this-voter differ when others discussed the target.
Both vote an accuser who blamed them for a prior elimination/bloc, but the specific accusation content differs.
Calling for a decisive vote vs proposing an evaluation structure, both ending in abstention.
Advocating a discussion topic vs proposing an evaluation method, both then abstaining.
Demanding on-record transparency vs proposing an analysis method, both then abstaining.
Preaching evidence-over-rash-accusation vs preaching current-over-past, both then voting.
Questioning an accuser then voting is ambiguous as to whether the accuser or the accused is voted.
Abstaining while citing insufficient evidence (the act) vs advocating abstention for insufficient info (the proposal).
Silent join framed around a role-accusation vs a generic silent join of the consensus.
Voting while acknowledging risk generally vs voting the consensus target despite hesitation about the evidence.
Voting the person who just voted for you (mutual vote) vs voting a verbal accuser.
Off-consensus vote justified by prior personal scrutiny vs a bare deviation from the majority.
Joining a bloc after debating a candidate's logic vs voting the person one was arguing with.
Voting immediately after initiating suspicion vs voting immediately after accusing of driving an elimination.
